title: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to the City Zero
summary: Given a tree with n cities and n-1 roads, where each road connects two cities, reorient some roads so that all cities can reach city 0.
statement: Given a tree with n cities and n-1 roads, where each road connects two cities, reorient some roads so that all cities can reach city 0. Return the minimum number of road directions that need to be changed. Each city must be able to travel to city 0, and it is assured that every city can reach city 0 after reordering.
constraints: The underlying undirected graph is a tree, while each connection has its listed direction.
Reverse the fewest edges so every city can follow directed roads to city zero.
hints: View the connections as an undirected tree rooted at zero while remembering each original direction.
Traversing from zero to a child costs one reversal exactly when the original edge points parent-to-child.
Sum those costs in DFS or BFS.
Every non-root node has one parent edge and must use it toward zero, so each incorrect edge is independently necessary and sufficient to reverse.
editorial: Every non-root node has one parent edge and must use it toward zero, so each incorrect edge is independently necessary and sufficient to reverse.

tests.explanation: Three edges point away from zero in the rooted traversal and must reverse.
Two listed directions oppose travel toward zero.
